subjects.displayTitle: Realms of being: widening the horizon of existence
subjects.introduction: A mineral has no idea that plants exist; a plant knows nothing of the animal; and the animal cannot guess at a mind that lays plans for a continent it has never seen. All of them share one world. That is how ‘Abdu’l-Bahá answers the question of where the next world is: existence is a single world whose stations differ, and a station we cannot perceive is not therefore absent. The worlds of God are countless, Bahá’u’lláh says, though some name four, or three, or five; the Báb speaks of eternity, perpetuity and time, and the ringstone symbol draws the worlds of God, of Command and of creation as three lines joined by grace. Each name takes its meaning inside its own explanation or prayer, and every account bows before an Essence no knowledge can reach. Jesus’s promise of many dwelling places in the Father’s house, and His answer to Thomas about the way, hold the same question in a Christian voice [1]. What is formed here, in capacity, attachment and virtue, is what travels on. The journey continues into the degrees of spirit and the kingdoms of existence, the ringstone symbol, and the Kingdom of God itself.
subjects.arc: Begin with the possibility of another level within one existence, distinguish spiritual perception from physical location, then explore the varied accounts of realms through transcendence, revelation, growth, and prayer.

order.why: Consider the four named worlds without treating them as an exhaustive inventory.
shortened: Though the worlds of God be infinite, yet some refer to them as four: the world of time, which hath both a beginning and an end; the world of duration, which hath a beginning but whose end is not apparent; the world of primordial reality, whose beginning is not to be seen but which is known to have an end; and the world of eternity, of which neither the beginning nor the end is visible.
Others have called these the worlds of the Heavenly Court, of the Celestial Dominion, of the Divine Kingdom, and of Mortal Existence.

order.why: Open with the reported museum conversation and the image of going upstairs.
Explore many conditions within one world of existence.
shortened: Now the greatest doubt of the deniers is this: where is that world? And everything which has no concrete external existence is mere imagination. However, the world of existence is one world, but it becomes manifold in relation to diverse realities. For example, the mineral, vegetable and animal worlds are one world, but the animal world in relation to the vegetable world is a spiritual reality and another realm, another condition.

order.why: Read the question of place through differing capacities of perception.
shortened: But if ye ask as to the place, know ye that the world of existence is a single world, although its stations are various and distinct. For example, the mineral life occupieth its own plane, but a mineral entity is without any awareness at all of the vegetable kingdom, and indeed, with its inner tongue denieth that there is any such kingdom. In the same way, a vegetable entity knoweth nothing of the animal world, remaining completely heedless and ignorant thereof, for the stage of the animal is higher than that of the vegetable, and the vegetable is veiled from the animal world and inwardly denieth the existence of that world---all this while animal, vegetable and mineral dwell together in the one world.

order.why: Establish the countlessness of the worlds of God.
Read the three worlds through the ringstone symbol’s account of grace.
Distinguish degrees of existence from infinite perfections.
shortened: Know that the degrees of existence are finite--the degrees of servitude, of prophethood and of Divinity--but that the perfections of God and of creation are infinite.

order.why: Place the limits of comprehension before more detailed metaphysical accounts.
shortened: As to the attributes and perfections such as will, knowledge, power and other ancient attributes that we ascribe to that Divine Reality, these are the signs that reflect the existence of beings in the visible plane and not the absolute perfections of the Divine Essence that cannot be comprehended.

order.why: Distinguish the Primal Will from the unknowable divine Essence.
shortened: As to the station of the Godhead, it is exalted above and sanctified beyond the understanding of all created things, how much more above resolving itself into their realities!  His Holiness the Bab (may my life be a sacrifice unto Him) hath stated that the meaning of the verse "The sea hath ever been the sea, and all contingent things its waves and forms" is fulfilled in the Primal Will, not in the Divine Essence.

order.why: Read the contrast between uncaused divine and dependent created existence.
shortened: Existence is of two kinds: One is the existence of the True One (God) which is sanctified above the comprehension of creation. He is the Unknowable Invisible. He is not preceded by any cause, but rather is the Creator of the Cause of causes. He is Ancient without beginning and absolutely Self-Sufficient. The second existence is that of creation. It is a general existence which is a mental concept that human reason can comprehend. This existence is originated, dependent, preceded by cause, and contingent.

order.why: Consider Command as the mediating reality in a threefold account.
shortened: But in the view of the Prophets it is not so. Rather, through proofs and evidences they established a third realm: the world of Truth [Haqq; also God], the world of Command, and the world of creation.

The world of Command is the station of the Primal Will which is a universal reality that is resolved into infinite forms. This is the reality of existence that is comprehended and understood by the human world. As for the world of creation, it consists of the infinite forms of that sea of Will which is the world of Command.

order.why: Keep the comparison with Sufi thought within this passage’s own philosophical argument.
Read giver, grace, and recipient as three related terms.
shortened: But as to the question of the Trinity, know, O advancer unto God, that in each one of the cycles wherein the Lights have shone forth upon the horizons (i. e., in each prophetic dispensation) and the Forgiving Lord hath revealed Himself on Mount Paran (see Habbakkuk 3:3, etc.) or Mount Sinai, or Mount Seir (see Ezekiel 35), there are necessarily three things: The Giver of Grace, and the Grace, and the Recipient of the Grace; the Source of the Effulgence, and the Effulgence, and the Recipient of the Effulgence; the Illuminator, and the Illumination, and Illuminated.

order.why: Consider the Primal Veil in the Bab’s account.
Enter the Tablet of All Food’s distinct stations while preserving its personal lament.
shortened: Among them is the Paradise of Oneness, the Yellow Land, the Ocean of Jabarut. This is the station of "Thou art He and He is thou" - servants who speak not save by God's leave, who act not save by His command, and who forbid not save by His decree, even as God hath described them: "honored servants who precede Him not in speech and who act by His command."

Among them is the station of the Paradise of Grace, the Crimson Land, the mystery of the Yellow, the hidden secret of the White, the Point of Nasut. Verily the evidences of remembrance therein are greatest, did ye but know.

If the Primal Point were alive in these days and witnessed My grief he would assuredly, at all times, comfort Me, treat Me tenderly, and fill Me with ardent joy. At every moment would he strengthen Me. Alas, alas! Would that I had died after him before these days, or had become a thing forgotten, utterly forgotten!

order.why: Read eternity, perpetuity, and time in the Bab’s explanation.
Retain the prayer’s ordered allusions and its insistence on what exceeds knowledge.
Read the Bab’s letter symbolism and numerical account in its own terms.
shortened: Know thou that every letter thereof hath seven stations---those stations which the Imam, in the realm of recognition, enjoined upon Jabir, when He said (exalted be His remembrance) unto the end of the tradition. And for each of these stations there are the four worlds, which in certain places are expressed as: the Lahut, which is the rank of the heart, and the first atom; the Jabarut, which is the station of the intellect, and the second; the Mulk, which is the station of the soul and the third scene, and the Word of tahlil; and the Malakut, which is the station of the Proof and the fourth scene, and the Word of takbir.

order.why: Consider the caution about describing a higher world through a lower one.
shortened: The description of each subsequent world describes the nature of the world before it unto the end of its station. Therefore it is related in the tradition that the ant claims for God two lordships, and that description which is in everything is God's lordship over it thereby.

order.why: Follow the Word through the named stages of its manifestation.
Names and distinguishes four realms of being.
Read the differing designations within the passage’s symbolic language.
Consider names according to different realms and manifestations.
Read the relation of elemental signs and the enduring spiritual reality.
shortened: The divine worlds are infinite. One world among the worlds of God is this elemental world, which is but a sign of other worlds. But those of limited vision, lacking spiritual insight, imagine that existence is confined to the material realm and thus become veiled from the worlds of God by earthly conditions.

order.why: Explore the soul’s ascent and the distinct account of the Divine Soul.
shortened: And when the soul hath unfolded the wings of the spirit, been attracted by the Joy of God, hath soared to the most exalted horizon, hath sought the most glorious Companion (rafiq al-abha), it doth ascend to the divine station of Jabarut (the realm of Command) and is assisted by an overwhelming and all-conquering power and by the intricate and ancient secret and by the noble and mighty mystery. It becomes aware of the secrets of hidden and invisible realities which consumes in envy the hearts of the mystic knowers. It is imprinted by the rays shining forth from the Sun of Truth and by its effects and comes to resemble its appearance and its light in every state and condition.

And as for "the Divine Soul" (an-nafs al-ilahiyyah), it consists of the Universal Reality which brings together all of the Divine realities of the realm of Primal Manifestation (lahutiyyah) and the eternal secrets, the outer aspect of which is the ancient light and the inner aspect is the most mighty and sublime mystery, the Primal Point from which appear all things and to which they revert, from which they originate and to which they return. Thus is it the Primal Oneness (al-ahadiyyah) in its essence and the derived Oneness (al-wahidiyyah) in its attributes.

order.why: Distinguish divine assistance from the heavenly spirit specific to the Prophets.
shortened: The divine spirit which is from God's command refers to the holy power, divine confirmations, eternal assistance, divine knowledge and heavenly sciences with which God aids whomever He wishes among His righteous servants.

The heavenly spirit is a holy essence, a perfect word, a complete sign, the mystery of existence and the reality hidden from the eyes of all beings. It is the Supreme Pen, the Divine Soul, and the manifestation of Truth from the dawning-place of creation and its sun at the dayspring of invention. This is specific to the Prophets in the worlds of creation.

order.why: Consider existence as one concept with differing capacities and determinations.
shortened: This matter is correct, but what is meant by spirit is existence and life, for existence has a single concept that is not multiple. Existence has ranks, and in each rank it has determination, individuation and special capacity. For example, the mineral, plant, animal and human realms are all in the realm of existence, and none of these realities is deprived of that concept. However, existence has manifestation, emergence and conditions in each of these ranks.

order.why: Read the public address’s account of spirit manifest in degrees.
shortened: The greatest power in the realm and range of human existence is spirit -- the divine breath which animates and pervades all things. It is manifested throughout creation in different degrees or kingdoms.

order.why: Keep the reported natural analogies in their historical philosophical setting.
shortened: I thought of how the spirit radiates in all the realms of nature according to the receptive degree. In the mineral world the spirit shows itself, but limited to that mineral condition. It is proved through science that the mineral has the power of attraction, the vegetable has the power of growth; life is according to capacity.

order.why: Read the reported human relation to the other kingdoms.
shortened: Regard this globe. Its divisions are mineral, vegetable and animal. Man is the result of all these; therefore man is the result of all existence here.

order.why: Consider the reported distinction between sensory and intellectual knowing.
shortened: The contingent world is in two great divisions--the physical and the mental.
The material or physical world or the "world of sense" is comprehended through the five senses, but the intellectual world is comprehended through the instrumentality of knowledge.

order.why: Read derived light and light itself as analogies in this account.
Explore the public address’s terminology for three human realities.
Retain the distinct three-mold account and its emphasis on choice.
Read the reported natures through the divine qualities a person imparts.
shortened: Man may be said to have three natures: The first is sunk in darkness and here he is a prisoner to his desires for here he is co-possessor of the same qualities as the animals. The second nature might be called his human nature and in this human nature is the home of the mind and the soul. The third is his likeness to God and this he possesses in proportion to the divine qualities he imparts, the breeze of the holy spirit, pure spiritually, luminosity.

order.why: Consider the reported contrast between the Absolute and created dependence.
Keep the reported comparisons with other traditions attributed rather than equating all systems.
shortened: We, of the Orient, distinguish between the wholly transcendent Primal Deity, in the Christian sense God the Father, and the Logos (Gospel of St. John, chapt. 1, verses 1 and 2), in the Christian sense God the Son, also called Demiurge (in the sense of the Greek philosophers), also called the Primal Will by His Holiness the Bab and designated by the Sufis (religious brotherhood) by the name of tawhid = oneness.

order.why: Read the reported challenge to confining existence to the material universe.
shortened: Those who lack wisdom think that the worlds of God are limited to the material universe. They deny that there are spiritual realms.

order.why: Hear the separate reported affirmation of many unseen worlds.
Read the reported allusion to the Father’s many mansions.
shortened: "Why should you wish to return here? In My Father's House are many mansions -- many, many worlds! Why should you desire to come back to this particular planet?"

order.why: Consider the reported worlds of qualities rather than places.
Explore the account of past, present, and future in the realm of truth.
shortened: Likewise, in the realm of truth, past, present, and future are the same, and future events are even as past and present occurrences. From the perspective of that realm, all events and incidents take place in the present and are witnessed by the Prophets and the chosen ones. And so it is that the Prophets herald events that will transpire two or three thousand years hence, for they abide in the realm of truth, wherein the mysteries of the universe are revealed and laid bare.

order.why: Read comprehension’s limits through the image of fettered wings.
shortened: The pinions of those nigh unto God, despite all their ardor and ecstasy, their attraction and rapture, are debarred from this atmosphere, and the wings of men are bound and fettered. No thought or knowledge or intelligence can traverse beyond heaven and earth - all that exists lieth between these twain. Yet the guardians of the pavilion of grandeur and the sentinels of the sanctuaries of the Kingdom exist above a hundred thousand visible worlds. This heaven, compared to that heaven, is as the earth before this heaven - nay, I seek God's forgiveness from every limitation and delimitation. The fettered wing knoweth not how to soar, and wings besmeared with clay cannot transcend their bounds.

order.why: Retain the appeal to what lies beyond present comprehension.
shortened: If such is what will take place in this visible world, then imagine what it will be in the spiritual realms of God, so exalted above the comprehension of all beings.

order.why: Consider the contingent world as a drop beside the Placeless.
Hear the contrast between earthly restriction and the birds of the Kingdom.
shortened: You well know that the realm of earthly existence is confined and restricted, and that the birds of the Kingdom have clipped wings therein.

order.why: Read the reported world as a place of preparation and developing consciousness.
shortened: This is the matrix world for the soul, even as the womb was the matrix world for the body or vehicle. - Birth into consciousness of another world begins here, a world for which this physical and material one is but the preparation and foundation."

order.why: Keep the reported account of purification through mercy and bounty.
shortened: Not on  the earthly planet does this development and purification of the imperfectly matured souls take place, but in the uncounted spiritual worlds of God; also not out of own endeavor and tiring penance, but in the creative light, in the purifying mercy and the purifying bounty of God, the Eternal, Almighty, and All-kind.

order.why: Read the address to Breakwell through love and hope beyond death.
shortened: O Breakwell, O my dear one!
Thou hast quit this earthly world and risen upward to the Kingdom, thou hast reached unto the grace of the invisible realm, and offered thyself at the threshold of its Lord.

order.why: Consider the movement from darkness toward light.
shortened: For they have hastened from the world of darkness to the world of light, and pitched their tent in the precincts of the Throne of the All-Merciful.

order.why: Retain the brief account of journeying between material and spiritual experience.
shortened: You will witness freedom in both worlds and agility in every arena. At times you will traverse the realm of the material world, at times you will journey through the Kingdom. Sometimes you will hasten to the heights of evanescence, sometimes you will race into the depths of effacement and nothingness.

order.why: Read the present world as a place where consequences may remain hidden.
shortened: O thou who hast believed in God! When, in the desert of deprivation, the intensity of thy thirst increased, thou didst hasten to the fountainhead of the Water of Life and didst drink from the Spring of the All-Merciful. Seek thou the effects of this heavenly sustenance in the realm of the Kingdom, and search after the outpourings of this divine reality in the desert of the invisible Empyrean. For this earthly abode is a place of concealment, not of manifestation, and a station of weakness, not of perceiving the results of all things.

order.why: Connect spiritual perception with the cleansing of its channel.
shortened: Know then that the Lord God possesseth invisible realms which the human intellect can never hope to fathom nor the mind of man conceive. When once thou hast cleansed the channel of thy spiritual sense from the pollution of this worldly life, then wilt thou breathe in the sweet scents of holiness that blow from the blissful bowers of that heavenly land.

order.why: Bring the inquiry to the heart’s freedom from envy.
Read the account of love between God and creatures.
shortened: And similarly, some of those who dwell among the sanctified signs consider that the Love of the True One for the creatures is the appearance of the effulgences of the Divinity [uluhiyyat] and the continuance of the attributes of the Heavenly Realm [lahutiyyat] in the temples and places of manifestation of the physical world [nasutiyya].  The Love of the servant for the Absolute is the annihilation of the existence and the passing away of the attributes of the physical world in Heavenly Perpetuation [baqa-yi lahutiyya] and Divine Manifestations.

order.why: Consider the reported permanence of ethical and moral teachings.
Hear the reported prayer for insight and confirmation.
shortened: I constantly pray for you and beg for each the divine Confirmations, so that the eyes of your insight may be opened and thus be enabled to see those objects which are not seen by others, to feel those susceptibilities which are not felt by others, to be reinforced by the invisible powers, to become cognizant of the worlds of God, because the divine worlds are infinite.

order.why: Read the reported wings of abstraction, beatitude, and certainty.
Enter prayer through thirst, estrangement, sickness, and captivity.
shortened: I am sore athirst; give me to drink of the oceans of Thy bountiful favor. I am a stranger; draw me nearer unto the source of Thy gifts. I am sick; sprinkle upon me the healing waters of Thy grace. I am a captive; rid me of my bondage, by the power of Thy might and through the force of Thy will, that I may soar on the wings of detachment towards the loftiest summits of Thy creation.

order.why: Hear the petition by the signs and mysteries of Kingdom and Dominion.
shortened: I implore Thee by the signs of Thy Kingdom and the mysteries of Thy Dominion to do with Thy loved ones as becometh Thy bounty, O Lord of all being, and is worthy of Thy grace, O King of the seen and the unseen!

order.why: Read the prayer for cleansing, nearness, and enduring life.
Hold the prayer for forgiveness beside its account of suffering.
shortened: Sprinkle, O my Lord, upon them from the ocean of Thy forgiveness what will make them worthy to abide, so long as Thine own sovereignty endureth, within Thy most exalted kingdom and Thine all-highest dominion.

He, round whose person circleth Thy proof, and in whose name and on behalf of whose sovereignty Thy testimony crieth out unto all created things, hath suffered more grievously in his days than any pen can recount, and been so harassed that He Who is Thy Spirit (Jesus) lamented, and all the denizens of Thy Kingdom and all the inmates of Thy Tabernacle in the realms above cried with a great and bitter lamentation.

order.why: Consider steadfastness awakening longing and prayer for knowledge.
shortened: Through His immovable constancy in Thy Cause, and His unwavering adherence to whatsoever Thou, in the plentitude of the light of Thy glory, didst unveil to His eyes, throughout the domains of Thy Revelation and creation, the souls of Thy servants were stirred up in their longing for Thy Kingdom, and the dwellers of Thy realms rushed forth to enter into Thy heavenly dominion.

Cast upon this poor and desolate creature, O my Lord, the glance of Thy wealth, and flood his heart with the beams of Thy knowledge, that he may apprehend the verities of the unseen world, and discover the mysteries of Thy heavenly realm, and perceive the signs and tokens of Thy kingdom, and behold the manifold revelations of this earthly life all set forth before the face of Him Who is the Revealer of Thine own Self.

order.why: Read the First Word’s renewing influence across the realms.
shortened: I testify that no sooner had the First Word proceeded, through the potency of Thy will and purpose, out of His mouth, and the First Call gone forth from His lips than the whole creation was revolutionized, and all that are in the heavens and all that are on earth were stirred to the depths. Through that Word the realities of all created things were shaken, were divided, separated, scattered, combined and reunited, disclosing, in both the contingent world and the heavenly kingdom, entities of a new creation, and revealing, in the unseen realms, the signs and tokens of Thy unity and oneness.

order.why: Return to the limits of praise before the creative command.
shortened: How can, then, such a man succeed in befittingly extolling the One through a motion of Whose finger all the names and their kingdom were called into being, and all the attributes and their dominion were created, and Who, through yet another motion of that same finger, hath united the letters B and E (Be) and knit them together, manifesting thereby what the highest thoughts of Thy chosen ones who enjoy near access to Thee are unable to grasp, and what the profoundest wisdom of those of Thy loved ones that are wholly devoted to Thee are powerless to fathom.

order.why: Hear the springtime prayer for the fruits of holiness.
shortened: Magnified, O Lord my God, be Thy Name, whereby the trees of the garden of Thy Revelation have been clad with verdure, and been made to yield the fruits of holiness during this Springtime when the sweet savors of Thy favors and blessings have been wafted over all things, and caused them to bring forth whatsoever had been preordained for them in the Kingdom of Thine irrevocable decree and the Heaven of Thine immutable purpose.

order.why: Read the Divine Springtime’s celebration of the earth.
shortened: This is the Day whereon the unseen world crieth out: "Great is thy blessedness, O earth, for thou hast been made the footstool of thy God, and been chosen as the seat of His mighty throne." The realm of glory exclaimeth: "Would that my life could be sacrificed for thee, for He Who is the Beloved of the All-Merciful hath established His sovereignty upon thee, through the power of His Name that hath been promised unto all things, whether of the past or of the future."

order.why: Consider the stated purpose across earthly, celestial, and highest realms.
Retain the rhetorical question concerning revelation and sovereignty.
Read the tribute to a Tablet through its allusions to the realms.
shortened: Then remind the letter Jim from Us and give him glad tidings of a holy, preserved tablet which We have sent down unto him, a single letter of which cannot be equaled by all that hath been created in the realm of Lahut, then in the realm of Jabarut, then in the realm of Malakut, then in the heavens and earths.

order.why: Keep the devotional images of yearning in their original voice.
shortened: The inhabitants of the realms of My eternity, the dwellers of the cities of My immortality, and the companions of the depths of My grandeur yearn to meet this servant, and around him circle the Houris of the chambers of My paradise and the chaste maidens of My garden of paradise and good-pleasure.

order.why: Consider the Word’s gift of life and the image of detachment.
Close the linked readings with the invitation toward an enduring Kingdom.
shortened: Ascend, O people, unto My Kingdom which perisheth not, then behold the lights of your Lord's countenance which fade not away.

order.why: Retain the supplied Plotinus fragment with its original boundary.
Read the supplied three principles in their Neoplatonic setting.
Keep the supplied Mulla Sadra passage and its secondary transmission distinct.
Consider the supplied Hermetic account on its own terms.
Read the supplied scholarly summary of five planes without imposing it on every passage.
shortened: In the Sufi world-view, five 'worlds' ('awalim) or five basic planes of Being are distinguished, each one of them representing a Presence or an ontological mode of the absolute Reality in its self-manifestation. (1) The plane of the Essence (dhat), the world of the absolute non-manifestation (al-ghayb al-mutlaq) or the Mystery of Mysteries. (2) The plane of the Attributes and the Names, the Presence of Divinity (uluhiyah). (3) The plane of the Actions, the Presence of Lordship (rububiyah). (4) The plane of Images (amthal) and Imagination (khayal). (5) The plane of the senses and sensible experience (mushahadah). These five planes constitute among themselves an organic whole, the things of a lower plane serving as symbols or images for the things of the higher planes."

order.why: Keep the supplied Ibn Arabi explanation of life and its recipient attributed.
Read the supplied ringstone explanation beside the linked account.
Consider the supplied letter about knowledge through the Manifestation.
shortened: ...the gnostics maintain the existence of only two worlds, the world of God and the world of the creature. The prophets, however, maintained the existence of three worlds: the world of God, the world of the Will or the Word, and the world of created things. The Prophets, therefore, maintained that a knowledge of God is impossible.... There is, therefore, only one way to God and that is through the realization of His Manifestation or Prophet in that age.

order.why: Retain the provisional letter-symbolism excerpt and its incomplete citation boundary.
Read the supplied pilgrim note’s threefold account with its reported status.
Consider the supplied provisional passage on the spirit’s capacities.
Read the supplied Tablet to Varqa’s particular meanings of the realms.
Keep the provisional explanation of decree and limitation in its own terms.
End with the supplied account of this life as the place to acquire enduring capacities.

questions: How might a difference in capacity make one world seem like several distinct worlds?
What do the various accounts of three, four, or more realms illuminate, and what would be lost by forcing them into a single scheme?
How do the readings distinguish knowledge of divine signs from comprehension of the divine Essence?
What does John 14:1–6 bring to questions of dwelling, reunion, and finding a way?
How might worlds of love, knowledge, and purity become recognizable in present experience?
What qualities would you want to cultivate here if this life prepares capacities whose full significance is still unseen?

references.label: 1 · John 14:1–6 · The Father’s house and the question of the way
references.note: Read the King James Version’s promise of many dwelling places, reunion, and Jesus’s response to Thomas about the way to the Father. Compare its language of relationship and destination with the compilation’s discussions of worlds, spiritual capacity, and mediation. The passage is a Christian account in its own setting, rather than a direct equivalence for every Baha’i description of realms.

subjects.displayTitle: The Word of God: recognition, meaning, and transforming power
subjects.introduction: A reader who grasps the meaning of a line of Shakespeare is glad, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, and then He asks how much greater the gladness of one who perceives the reality hidden in the Holy Scriptures. The incomparability of the Word of God begins there, in a joy of understanding rather than in a contest of eloquence. Bahá’u’lláh describes the Word as prior to syllable and sound altogether, the Command of God pervading all created things, so that the verses on a page are the visible edge of something that gives sight to the blind and life to the dead, bread of heaven to the hungry and a cup of knowledge to those lost in ignorance. Beside the revealed verses, He says, every other proof is a star beside the sun. The Báb pressed the point as a challenge, as the Qur’án once did: let all who dwell on earth combine to produce a single verse like these, and they will not be able [1]. A word of the divine utterance outweighs the whole world, and the fitting answer to such a gift is gratitude that becomes understanding, detachment and action. The search widens from here into the Word as its own standard, the Word as the cause of creation, the many meanings folded within a single verse, and the influence that places the Word at the centre of a life.
subjects.arc: Begin with the joy of understanding and the Word beyond sound, explore nourishment and transformation, then read the claims of inimitability, spiritual value, and grateful response.

order.why: Establish the Word’s meaning beyond syllables and sound.
shortened: Know thou, moreover, that the Word of God - exalted be His glory - is higher and far superior to that which the senses can perceive, for it is sanctified from any property or substance. It transcendeth the limitations of known elements and is exalted above all the essential and recognized substances. It became manifest without any syllable or sound and is none but the Command of God which pervadeth all created things.

order.why: Open with the joy of understanding rather than mere possession of words.
shortened: May your souls be illumined by the light of the Words of God, and may you become repositories of the mysteries of God, for no comfort is greater and no happiness is sweeter than spiritual comprehension of the divine teachings. If a man understands the real meaning of a poet's verses such as those of Shakespeare, he is pleased and rejoiced. How much greater his joy and pleasure when he perceives the reality of the Holy Scriptures and becomes informed of the mysteries of the Kingdom!

order.why: Read the reported life-giving effects and the path of love.
shortened: What is truth? Truth is the word of God, which gives life to humanity. It restores sight to the blind and hearing to the deaf; it makes eloquent those who are dumb, and living beings out of dead beings; it illumines the world of heart and soul; it reduces into nothingness the iniquities of the neglectful and erring ones.
The road to attain to this Truth is the love of God. When the light of the love of God is burning in the mirror of the heart, that flame shows the way and guides to the Kingdom of the Word of God.

order.why: Explore the Book of Certitude’s nourishment, meaning, proof, and transcendence.
shortened: They have even failed to realize, all this time, that, in every age, the reading of the scriptures and holy books is for no other purpose except to enable the reader to apprehend their meaning and unravel their innermost mysteries.
For compared with all other proofs and tokens, the divinely revealed verses shine as the sun, whilst all others are as stars.
They are the treasury of the divine pearls and the depository of the divine mysteries.

Through them floweth the river of divine knowledge, and gloweth the fire of His ancient and consummate wisdom. This is the fire which, in one and the same moment, kindleth the flame of love in the breasts of the faithful, and induceth the chill of heedlessness in the heart of the enemy.

order.why: Consider inner meanings through the traces of the Pen.
Hear the public address’s description of wisdom, knowledge, and truth.
Receive the word as bounty inviting contentment and gratitude.
Read the unveiling of favor together with the question of one’s response.
Consider the Bab’s account of the verses as distinctive divine testimony.
shortened: In this Revelation the Lord of the universe hath deigned to bestow His mighty utterances and resplendent signs upon the Point of the Bayan, and hath ordained them as His matchless testimony for all created things. Were all the people that dwell on earth to assemble together, they would be unable to produce a single verse like unto the ones which God hath caused to stream forth from the tongue of the Point of the Bayan. Indeed, if any living creature were to pause to meditate he would undoubtedly realize that these verses are not the work of man, but are solely to be ascribed unto God, the One, the Peerless, Who causeth them to flow forth from the tongue of whomsoever He willeth, and hath not revealed nor will He reveal them save through the Focal Point of God's Primal Will.

order.why: Read the Seven Proofs on the Quran’s place as proof.
Hear the Bab’s challenge concerning the sufficiency of the Book.
shortened: Say: God is the Hidden of all hidden, if ye be of them that magnify His remembrance. Doth not that Book suffice you wherein is the decree of all things? Will ye not then be thankful? Say: A single verse sufficeth as a proof from God unto all who are in the heavens and on the earth and whatsoever lieth between them, would ye but know it.

order.why: Read the Epistle to Muhammad Shah’s appeal to the Quranic precedent.
Consider the epistle’s claim of proof and challenge to imitation.
shortened: Know thou that a single verse of what We have revealed unto thee sufficeth as proof for all who dwell on earth, and God is the All-Witnessing, the All-Knowing.

Should men and jinn combine to produce the like of this Book, and should the jinn assist them in their weakness, they would never be able, nor would they have the power, even were they to be helpers one of another.

order.why: Retain the Meccan proclamation’s formulation of the challenge.
Read the related address to Mulla Husayn.
Keep the separate letter from Bushihr in its original voice.
Consider the challenge joined to an invitation to enter the Gate.
Retain the statement of the challenge as a perfect proof.
shortened: Should all people gather together to produce the like of these verses, they would never be able, even if they were helpers one to another. This is a perfect proof from God's Book for all on earth, and God sufficeth as a witness over the worlds.

order.why: Read the question addressed to the Mufti of Baghdad.
shortened: Can any besides God reveal a single verse? Do you not see? If all who are on earth were to gather together to produce the like of this Book from God, they would never be able to do so, and God bears witness to this, as do those possessed of knowledge who are witnesses in God's religion.

order.why: Keep the related letter to the Hanafi Imam.
Read the extended challenge and its polemical argument without recasting it as an independent test result.
shortened: Read the Book We have sent down of nine hundred decisive verses, and traverse the east and west of the earth - if thou seest or hearest from anyone the like of one verse, then turn back from My Cause and seek what thou willest. Otherwise, God's conclusive proof is upon thee, just as the truth hath ever been conclusive through it.

order.why: Consider the distinction between imitation and spontaneous utterance in the Bab’s letter.
Keep the numerical and historical claims in the response’s own reasoning.
shortened: He himself hath witnessed to the number of one hundred thousand verses; and though all mankind, within the bounds wherein they stand, advance their claims, none hath been seen to bring the like. Is it that they are able yet refrain? Nay, for had it been in their power, long since would they have done so.

order.why: Retain the concise claim concerning producing a likeness.
Read the question about the source of such letters.
Keep the comparative claim concerning the Bab’s commentaries in its original wording.
Read the Bayan described as a book of encompassing laws.
Consider the account of proof and the quoted objections.
Read the appeal to those who witnessed the revelation of verses.
Hear the assertion that the revealed verses surpass enumeration.
Keep the reported judgments of translation, eloquence, and style attributed.
Read the reported musical analogy as a portrayal of spiritual distinction.
Consider the analogy of differing capacities and the limits of comprehension.
shortened: No lower thing can comprehend what is above it - just as the stone and tree, no matter how much they progress, cannot comprehend the reality of the animal, and the animal, no matter how much it progresses, cannot comprehend the reality of man. Thus man, no matter how much he progresses, cannot fathom the reality of the Word of God.

order.why: Read the claim that the Revelation exceeds the comprehension of books.
shortened: Say: By God! This is a Revelation which the Books have not comprehended, and which none hath understood save His Self, the One Who dominateth the worlds.

order.why: Keep the sharp admonition concerning minds in its own rhetorical voice.
Read the comparison of revelation with a sun among books.
shortened: O Shaykh! No breeze can compare with the breezes of Divine Revelation, whilst the Word which is uttered by God shineth and flasheth as the sun  amidst the books of men.

order.why: Hear the claim concerning even a single word.
shortened: The Word of God, even if limited to a single word, cannot be equaled by all the books of the world.

order.why: Consider the word beyond what minds have comprehended.
Read the worth of a letter through the condition of insight.
Explore the relation of incomparable worth and creative power.
Hear the declaration concerning a single letter of the revealed verses.
Retain the declaration concerning one letter from the Pen.
shortened: Say: By God! All who are in the heavens and earth cannot equal a single letter that proceedeth from My Pen, and I am the Bestower, the All-Bountiful, the Ancient of Days.

order.why: Read the distinction of verses in a personal address.
shortened: O emigrant! The divine verses are distinguished from all else - all that is mentioned and concealed between the heavens and earth cannot equal a single word thereof.

order.why: Hear the testimony concerning the books of the world.
shortened: Say: All the books of the world cannot compare with that which hath been sent down from His presence. To this beareth witness the Ancient King in His glorious and wondrous station.

order.why: Keep the claim of unparalleled disclosure in its original voice.
shortened: We have sent down in every matter that which cannot be equaled by aught revealed in creation, and I am verily the Truth, the Knower of things unseen.

order.why: Describes the unparalleled collective power of the Word of God.
Retain the concise comparison of a word and the entire world.
shortened: The entire world cannot equal a single word of the divine utterances.

order.why: Read the corresponding testimony of the Book and decree.
Hear the separate concise affirmation of incomparable worth.
shortened: The whole world cannot be compared to a single word from the divine utterances.

order.why: Read the value assigned to a word in the sight of God.
shortened: One word from the exalted utterances that appears from the Dayspring of the pronouncement of the Lord of Names is, in the sight of God - exalted be His glory - superior to all that is observed on earth.

order.why: Consider what lies in human hands beside the divine Word.
Retain the appeal to the testimony of scriptures.
Read the image of all creation filled with books yet unable to equal one letter.
Keep the claim concerning a Tablet together with its response to opposition.
Read the defense of the Bab within its account of injustice.
Consider the encompassing Book in relation to earlier scriptures.
shortened: All books are but a letter of this Book, and all scriptures proclaim His Name, the Guardian over all worlds.

order.why: Hear the declaration of the books’ submission.
Retain the rhetorical comparison with what was revealed before.
Read the testimony of the Mother Book to the new disclosure.
Keep the separate comparison with all earlier revelation.
shortened: Say: This is He, one word of Whose Book cannot be equaled
by all that was revealed aforetime.

order.why: Read the particular comparison with the Bayan.
shortened: The Beloved of creation declares: One word from the Divine Word in that Most Great Manifestation is better than all that was revealed in the Bayan.

order.why: Consider the personification of books bowing before revelation.
shortened: That which hath been sent down in truth causeth all the books of the world to bow down before it, did ye but know.

order.why: Distinguish acceptance from the mere memorization of every book.
shortened: The Mother Book calleth out with the most exalted voice and summoneth the people to the supreme horizon.

Whosoever hath attained unto acceptance and taken hold of it with the hand of certitude, he verily hath acknowledged and confessed all the divine Books. Without this, even if one were to memorize all Books, it would yield no fruit.

order.why: Read the claim to evidence and fair-minded recognition in its own voice.
Consider the reader’s eye of truth in evaluating a Tablet.
shortened: If thou observest with the eye of truth, thou wilt testify that nothing that is witnessed on earth can compare with this Tablet.

order.why: Read the ocean of meaning and the value perceived through insight.
Contrast enduring utterance with transient possessions.
shortened: All that is treasured in the coffers of kings and rulers cannot be compared with a single word from the divine utterances, for worldly ornaments, adornments and riches are transient and will return to nothingness, while that which floweth from the Most Exalted Pen endureth throughout the dominion of earth and heaven.

order.why: Retain the comparison with royal treasures.
shortened: By the life of God! Neither the riches of the world nor whatsoever is with the kings and rulers can equal one word thereof.

order.why: Read the separate declaration concerning earthly hoards.
Consider pearls and mines as images of material value.
shortened: By the life of God! The pearls in the ocean's shells and all that lies hidden in the mines cannot compare with My utterance.

order.why: Read the personal Tablet as a treasure beyond comparison.
shortened: This is a Tablet that cannot be equaled by the treasures of the world nor matched by the books of all creation.

order.why: Read the care owed to preserving the Book, keeping its source omission visible.
Connect a received Tablet with turning toward God.
Hear remembrance as an occasion for rejoicing and praise.
shortened: The traveler mentioned thee, and this Most Holy, Most Exalted Tablet, with which the entire world cannot compare even with a single letter thereof, hath been revealed that thou mayest rejoice thereat and speak forth the praise of God, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Read gratitude for being addressed by the Beloved.
shortened: Be thou grateful that thou hast been mentioned by the tongue of the Beloved, and that this Book hath been sent down unto thee, whereunto nothing in the heavens and the earth can compare.

order.why: Keep the striking comparison concerning remembrance and descendants in its own setting.
shortened: By the Sun of the horizon of sanctification! If but one word proceedeth from the Supreme Pen concerning a soul, it is more precious than a hundred thousand righteous children.

order.why: Consider remembrance and the grace of a single letter.
shortened: Blessed is the state of those souls who have attained to the remembrance of God in His days and have been honored with the sprinkling drops from the ocean of His grace, for a single letter from Him is more exalted and mightier than the creation of all things.

order.why: Read the word as water of life and sign of guidance.
Retain the comparison with deeds and morals without turning it into a denial of responsibility.
Hear the oath concerning what can be witnessed and what is spoken.
shortened: I swear by the lights of His countenance that whatsoever is witnessed cannot be compared with a single word from the words of God.

order.why: Read the concise testimony to a peerless revelation.
Retain the reported comparison with many volumes of wisdom.
shortened: One Book or Tablet of the Blessed Perfection is more comprehensive than fifty volumes of the world' s greatest wisdom.

order.why: Consider the reported challenge to upbuild the Cause with faith and love.
Close the linked readings with the Word as testimony to the worlds.
shortened: By God! A single letter thereof is better for thee than all that hath been created on earth, and none deny this save the wicked and the remote. Say: Verily the Word of God is the most exalted, and it is God's testimony unto all the worlds.

order.why: Read the supplied historical challenge beside its approximate catalogue reference.
End with the supplied claim that even a familiar term can bear unique distinction.

questions: What distinguishes appreciating beautiful language from responding to words as a divine address?
How does the description of a Word beyond syllables and sound change the inquiry into its incomparability?
What kinds of recognition, evidence, and response are brought together in the passages about revealed verses?
How does Qur’an 17:88 illuminate the challenge repeatedly expressed in the Bab’s writings?
What might the images of nourishment, light, water, and enduring treasure reveal about different effects of reading?
How could gratitude for a text’s spiritual value become understanding, detachment, and constructive action?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 17:88 · The challenge to produce a counterpart
references.note: Read Pickthall’s translation alongside the parallel renderings of the challenge to humanity and the jinn. Compare its formulation with the Bab’s repeated appeals to the Quranic precedent and with the compilation’s accounts of meaning and spiritual transformation. Distinguish the scriptural claim of inimitability from an editorial ranking of literary works.
